# Make the keyboard a first-class path

Every frequent action has a keyboard path whose shortcut is shown where the action appears; focus moves predictably and returns to its trigger when an overlay closes.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. Expert users rely on shortcuts they can discover in place, and lost focus after a dialog or menu closes strands keyboard and screen-reader users.

## Prefer

- Show the shortcut in the action's tooltip and menu item.
- Keep command palette names, shortcuts, and grouping identical to the menus they mirror.
- Move focus into an overlay when it opens and return it to the trigger when it closes.

## Avoid

- Shortcuts that exist only in documentation.
- Palette commands named differently from the same menu action.
- Dropping focus to the document start after closing a dialog, menu, or drawer.

## Use when

- A surface has frequent actions, overlays, menus, or a command palette.

## Do not use when

- A platform-native control already owns its keyboard behavior; follow the platform instead.

## Sources

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Keyboards — https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards

## Check

- Can every frequent action be reached by keyboard, and is its shortcut visible in place?
- Do palette entries match menu names and shortcuts?
- Does focus return to the trigger when each overlay closes?
